references.text: Despite oppression, the growth and strength of the people is a recurring theme in Exodus 1, where God's blessing over the Israelites continues.
Describes how the Israelites were fruitful, numerous, and very strong - the same pattern of growth confirmed in verse 20.
God's promise to Abraham to make him into a great nation is fulfilled through the people's growth in Egypt.
God's promise to multiply Abraham's descendants like the stars in the sky becomes visible in the Israelites' growth.
God's promise to Jacob to make him into a great nation in Egypt is fulfilled here.
Moses confirms that the Lord multiplied the people so they became as numerous as the stars in the sky.
The psalm describes how God made His people very fruitful and stronger than their enemies.
The righteous receive reward on earth - the midwives' fear of God was rewarded by Him.
Those who fear God prosper - the midwives' reverence for God led to His blessing.
Stephen's speech confirms that the people grew and became numerous in Egypt as the time for God's promise drew near.
The Hebrews mention the faith of the midwives, who did not fear the king's command, and God blessed them for it.
